synthesis.body: When a TOML emitter writes `installed-at = 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z` (bare offset-datetime literal), `tomllib.loads` parses that as a Python `datetime`. If a *different* writer (adversarial, hand-edited, third-party) writes `installed-at = "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\nphantom = \"injected\""` (TOML basic-string position instead of bare datetime), `tomllib` parses the same key as a Python `str` containing a real newline and quote bytes. Bare re-emission `f"installed-at = {entry['installed-at']}"` then lands phantom TOML structure on the next round-trip — even though the first-write side is clean. The fix has two layers: (1) filter prior entries at read time, requiring `isinstance(value, datetime)` for any field that's spec'd as a bare datetime; drop or warn on mismatch. (2) Store new entries as `datetime` (not a strftime'd string) so the emit loop has one uniform type and always applies the canonical strftime itself. Bit us during round-3 adversarial review of the TOML-injection hardening PR; the pack-metadata side was already closed but the marker round-trip path was a separate vector. Generalises to any TOML field where the schema says 'bare type X' but the loader will accept 'basic-string containing arbitrary bytes' at the same key.

title: TOML datetime round-trip injection: a bare-datetime field can come back as `str` and carry phantom payload on re-emit
